preamble: Monophthongization of the falling diphthong ui to i, the rounded back nucleus being absorbed into the front offglide. It is a core development in Japonic: Proto-Japonic *ui yields i in Proto-Ryukyuan and the vowel i₂ in Old Japanese (later merged with i), producing alternations such as Old Japanese tuki₂ 'moon' beside bound tuku-. The same coalescence recurs in casual Tokyo-area speech, where adjectives in -ui are realized with long [iː] (warui > warii).

examples.to: tuki₂ (bound form tuku-, as in tukuyo 'moonlit night'); Modern Japanese tsuki
examples.note: Pre-Old Japanese *ui became the vowel i₂, which merged with i by Early Middle Japanese; the bound form preserves the original u.

examples.to: kami₂ (bound form kamu-); Modern Japanese kami

examples.note: Informal coalescence of adjective-final -ui into a long front vowel.
